subject: Urgent: Clearbridge reserved throughput shortfall & dedicated pool saturation
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@clearbridge.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: laura@clearbridge.com
Date: 2026-09-02T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production errors + latency spike (Clearbridge)

Hi Grace,

We started seeing a significant uptick in 5xx errors and end-to-end latency across our payment inference calls starting ~07:45 PT. Our dashboard shows average latency rising from ~220ms to >1.2s and a 5xx rate jumping to 3.8% (was ~0.1%). This is affecting checkout throughput — we are losing approvals.

Quick data:
- Peak QPS to Redwood endpoint: 320 (avg 210)
- Reserved QPS in contract: 250 (paid reserved capacity)
- Error spike coincides with sustained sustained concurrent sessions at ~480 tokens+ per request on REQ model

We need an immediate mitigation plan and visibility into whether this is Dedicated pool saturation or a routing regresssion. Can someone confirm capacity headroom and whether automatic fallbacks were exercised?

Samir
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir@clearbridge.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors + latency spike (Clearbridge)

Samir — thanks for the heads up and the quick metrics. We're on it.

Immediate steps we are taking:
1) David (ops) is validating Dedicated pool utilization and any token queueing.
2) Marissa (AM/CS) will coordinate a short mitigation plan and confirm whether we can route eligible calls to the lower-latency model variant with the same contract terms.
3) I'll scope a credit/compensation proposal if we confirm reserved throughput shortfall.

Can you share an example request id and timestamp range for a failed call? That will help trace through routing and kernel-level logs.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors + latency spike (Clearbridge)

Grace / Marissa — initial findings from the node telemetry and scheduler:
- Dedicated GPU pool (us-west-2, pool-id: dgp-7a) saw sustained GPU utilization at 98% between 07:40–08:20 PT.
- KV cache pressure increased; we observed higher eviction rates for long-session keys (median session length +75% vs baseline).
- Autoscaling attempted a single burst allocation but failed due to capacity ceiling on that host group; allocation rejected by infra policy (burst limit = 20% over reserved).
- Routing logs show ~18% of Clearbridge requests retried to fallback variants; fallback capacity was exhausted after 07:50.
- Error signature: transient OOM while spawining new worker threads under high concurrent KV warmups; manifests as 5xx with diagnostic id prefix CB-ERR-9.

Short-term mitigation I'm deploying now:
- Force-routing for Clearbridge: 40% of traffic to quantized lower-memory variant (rq-v2-q4) that preserves 98% of accuracy for payment scoring.
- Enable immediate aggressive KV eviction controls to reduce new-worker OOMs (tradeoff: longer cold-starts).

I'll post a follow-up in 20m with observed recovery metrics.

— David
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir@clearbridge.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors + latency spike (Clearbridge)

Samir — thank you for raising this. We're switching 40% to rq-v2-q4 as David notes and throttling lower-priority background jobs. Expecting immediate reduction in 5xx and median latency to return under 400ms.

Operational asks for Clearbridge:
- Please provision example request ids in the 07:40–08:05 PT window (even one will do).
- Agree to a short maintenance window tonight (23:00–23:30 PT) to temporarily raise burst limit and run a controlled warmup. That will require Exec approval on our side; copying Aditya to expedite.

If we can confirm root cause = dedicated pool oversubscription, we will propose either a temporary credit, a short-term burst add-on (metered), or a contract amendment to increase reserved QPS. We'll include clear SLAs for any change.

— Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors + latency spike (Clearbridge) — exec note

Looping in exec context:
- Summary: Dedicated pool saturation caused routing fallbacks and transient OOMs; Clearbridge observed >3% 5xx and throughput degradation vs contract (reserved 250 QPS).
- Business impact estimate (prelim): estimated failed approvals ~1.1k requests in the 40m window, revenue exposure $18k (rough estimate from Clearbridge volume).

Proposed immediate decisions we need:
1) Approve a one-off burst authorization to raise the pool ceiling by +30% for 3 hours tonight (engineering will run warmup and monitor). This would be billed as metered burst; we should offer a partial credit if we determine platform-side fault.
2) Approve a short credit (pro-rated month credit) if postmortem identifies insufficient routing/fallback automation.
3) Start contract amendment discussion for permanent reserve increase to 350 QPS or convert to Dedicated+ with guaranteed hot spares. Marissa please lead.

If agreed, I will coordinate finance/legal for a fast-track amendment and sign-off.

— Aditya
VP, Customer Reliability
From: Samir Patel <samir@clearbridge.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@clearbridge.com, laura@clearbridge.com
Date: 2026-09-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors + latency spike (Clearbridge) — acceptance of mitigation & asks

Thanks everyone for the quick response. Recovery looked better after the 40% reroute — latency median dropped to ~360ms and 5xx back under 0.3% within 18 minutes. We're amenable to the proposed maintenance window tonight (23:00 PT).

Two asks before we proceed:
1) We want a written commit that Clearbridge will not be billed for the metered burst if the postmortem attributes primary cause to Dedicated pool scheduling / eviction policies.
2) Please share the postmortem within 72 hours and a concrete guardrail plan (autoscale policy changes, priority routing exceptions, and a timeline for contract amendment)

Attached: sample request ids and a short clip from our monitoring (clearbridge_error_logs.zip).

Samir
Head of Platform Ops, Clearbridge Payments
